note:
THE SECOND PAPER, AND IT BRACKETS THE SCENE DATE. The American's first issue is 1835-06-08, three weeks before 1835-07-01, and the run continues to 1835-08-29. Its value is not that it repeats the Democrat: it is a SECOND, INDEPENDENT witness to the same town in the same weeks, from a different office with different advertisers. Where the two agree on an address, that address is as well attested as anything this project holds. Where they disagree, the disagreement is itself the finding and must be recorded, not resolved by preference.

RULING 2, THE OWNER'S, 2026-08-28, RECORDED VERBATIM AND BINDING ON EVERY CLAIM TAKEN FROM THIS PUBLICATION: "Transcription-mediated readings grade `documented`, carrying a flag. The corpus is read through OCR-assisted transcriptions, not the page scans. Every claim taken this way carries `reading: transcription_mediated` and preserves the transcription's own uncertainty brackets. This EXTENDS, and does not overturn, data/sources/chicago_democrat_1833_11_26.json's standard — where a scan exists and is read, the scan remains the authority (it caught 'C. & I. HARMON' where the transcription had 'C. & L. Harmon'), and a transcription-mediated claim upgrades when a scan read confirms it."

RULING 1, the owner's, 2026-08-28: "A letter-list name is enough to mint a resident" — recorded `letter_list_only: true`, so the two evidence strengths stay distinguishable forever. RULING 3, same day: "A documented business is BUILT at the scene date unless contradicted" — a dissolution, removal or replacement notice is the only thing that keeps one out of the 1835 town. Ruling 3 costs this publication almost nothing: its whole run sits within twelve weeks of the scene date, so its businesses need no survival liberty at all. That is the reason to reach for the American FIRST when a Democrat attestation is from 1833 or 1834.

THE TRAPS THIS PUBLICATION CONTAINS, restated corpus-wide from the per-issue record data/sources/chicago_democrat_1833_11_26.json, which found all three by reading the scan at 2.4x-9x. They are properties of 1830s jobbing printing and of bound volumes, not of one issue, so they apply to every issue in this run.

1. A STOCK CUT IS NOT A PICTURE OF A CHICAGO BUILDING. Nineteenth-century printers kept generic engravings for property, estray and shipping advertisements and struck the same block for any advertiser. No elevation, storey count, roof form or window arrangement may be taken from an engraving in this corpus, ever.

2. AD-COPY DATES ARE NOT ISSUE DATES. An advertisement carries the date its copy was written and ran for weeks or months afterwards. The date at the foot of an advertisement establishes when the trade was being carried on no later than — it does not establish that the advertiser was still there on the issue date, and it is not the issue's own date.

3. A LATER PENCILLED GLOSS IS NOT LETTERPRESS. A modern reader's marginal annotation in a bound volume can read as contemporary corroboration once it is transcribed. The motivating case is exact and it is in this run: an 'S. W.' pencilled in the right margin of the 1833-11-26 advertisement page, level with the Democrat's own imprint, which would silently promote the paper's office from a named JUNCTION to a named CORNER on no evidence at all. Quarantine every annotation that is not letterpress.

4. AND ONE THE CORPUS ADDS. The transcriptions carry the transcriber's own apparatus — headers, editorial-method paragraphs, `[uncertain: ...]`, `[illegible]`, `[missing at edge]` and per-column validation notices. None of it is 1830s type. A citation must name an issue page and column, which is exactly what the apparatus cannot supply.

THE CITATION CONVENTION, and it is a bar, not a suggestion: A CLAIM THAT CANNOT NAME ITS COLUMN CANNOT BE MADE. Cite, in this order — publication; issue date; volume and number as PRINTED; issue page and column, taken from the transcription's own `===== ISSUE PAGE n / PDF PAGE m / COLUMN k OF 6 =====` markers; then the transcription file path and the line range within it. Resolve the path through chicago/4d/data/research/newspapers/corpus.json, which is the register of every issue in this run and the only place the paths are guaranteed current. Preserve the transcription's uncertainty brackets inside any quotation; do not tidy them away. Where the printed volume or number is visibly wrong or repeated, transcribe what is printed and say so — the corpus workflow forbids silently repairing it, and this run repeats a number three times.

THE MASTHEAD OF THE FIRST ISSUE IS WRONG, AND THE PAPER SAYS SO ITSELF. The 1835-06-08 masthead prints May 8, 1835; the issue carries a correction stating that May 8 is an error and the date should be June 8, 1835. The printed form is transcribed and the correction is recorded — the date of that issue is 1835-06-08 on the paper's own authority, not on an editor's tidying.

AND A REPEATED NUMBER. Vol. I, No. 12 is printed on BOTH 1835-08-22 and 1835-08-29. Preserved, not renumbered. Cite an American issue by its DATE; the number does not identify it.

TRANSCRIPTION QUALITY: THIS IS THE WEAKER OF THE TWO RUNS, and a reader should know it before quoting. The whole American set is single-pass OCR with alternate segmentation on low-confidence columns — no reconciled second-reviewer pass, no manifest, no validation notes, and no committed .txt from the transcriber. Mastheads, imprints and headings come through clean; dense body columns are frequently unreadable, and the 1835-07-04 issue's first column opens 'aa of nik months. P until Ai] arrearager'. Treat a clean-reading heading or advertisement address as usable evidence and an unclear body passage as no evidence at all. Every American reading is `reading: transcription_mediated` and every one of them upgrades the day a scan is read.

WHERE THE TEXT IS. The archival transcriptions live at chicago/reference/newspapers/Transcriptions/ and are the owner's deposit, read-only to this project. They were committed to `main` on 2026-08-28 and are NOT on `dev`, where this subtree is developed, so a `dev` checkout cannot open them; T-0275 carries the back-merge, which is not trivial because `main` also carries sixty Finder-duplicate files under site/chicago/4d/data/ that turn this repo's gate red in twenty-three places. The twenty-three issues delivered as .docx only were extracted to chicago/4d/data/research/newspapers/text/ by tools/docx_text.py and ARE committed here, so those are citable on any branch.
access_notes: No committed .txt and no manifest were delivered with this run, so its text exists in this project only as the derived extraction under chicago/4d/data/research/newspapers/text/. Word counts and uncertainty-marker counts are therefore null in corpus.json for every American issue — absent, not zero. chicago/4d/data/research/ is research, never payload.
